sheets.title: Pallavas and Chalukyas of Badami (275 – 897 CE)
sheets.intro: Pallava kings, temples and villages; Badami Chalukyas, Aihole, Pattadakal.

keys.name: Early Pallavas (Andhra roots)
keys.hook: Mayidavolu in Guntur – Pallavas began in Andhra

rows.v: Lower Krishna valley – successors of Satavahanas, Ikshvakus
Mayidavolu plates of Shivaskandavarman (Guntur) – Prakrit; also Hirahadagalli
Sanskrit and Tamil in Pallava Grantha script (parent of SE Asian scripts)
Ghatika (temple college); Kadamba founder Mayurasharman studied there, quarrelled, set up his own kingdom
Beat the Kalabhras – imperial Pallava rule from Kanchi
Avanisimha (lion of the earth)
Bharavi – Kiratarjuniya
Mattavilasa, Chitrakarapuli (tiger among painters), Vichitrachitta, Gunabhara
Mattavilasa Prahasana (Sanskrit farce)
Mahendra style – first rock-cut temples; Mandagapattu inscription – temple without brick, timber, metal, mortar
Jain → Shaiva through Appar (Tirunavukkarasar)
Pullalur – clash with Pulakeshin II (start of Pallava – Chalukya wars)

keys.name: Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla)

rows.v: Killed Pulakeshin II, sacked Vatapi 642 (general Paranjothi) – "Vatapikonda"
Two invasions to restore prince Manavamma
Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram); Seven Rathas (monolithic – Dharmaraja, Bhima, Draupadi rathas); Arjuna's Penance relief; yali pillars, Varaha Mandapa
Hiuen Tsang at Kanchi, 642

traps: Rathas = Narasimhavarman I; Shore temple = Rajasimha

rows.v: c. 695 – 722 CE; peaceful
Rajasimha style – structural temples: Shore temple (Mahabalipuram, UNESCO; Shiva + Vishnu shrines), Kailasanatha (Kanchi; 16-sided linga; 58 small shrines)
Embassies
Dandin – Dashakumaracharita, Kavyadarsha
c. 731 – 796; Vaikuntha Perumal temple, Kanchi (Vishnu standing, sitting, lying; records his rise); Bhakti; village self-rule
Small plain temples – Mukteshwara, Matangeshwara
Vikramaditya II took Kanchi but spared it, gave gifts to Kailasanatha
c. 885 – Aparajitavarman beat the Pandyas
Aparajitavarman beaten by Aditya I Chola, late 9th c.
Dharma-Maharaja
Kottams (districts)
Sabha (Brahmadeya villages), Urar (ordinary villages); court Dharmasasana
Land revenue; taxes on professions, marriage, salt, cloth, cattle
Brahmadeya (tax-free to Brahmins); Eripatti (tank land for upkeep)
Manigramam (merchants)
Gold and silver later; barter earlier

keys.name: Pallava age religion and culture

rows.v: Shaiva and Vaishnava rise; Buddhism, Jainism fall
12 Vishnu saints; Andal only woman; Nalayira Divya Prabandham (4,000 hymns)
63 Shiva saints; Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar – Tevaram (start of Tirumurai)
Advaita
Yaazhi (harp), Mridangam, Murasu (war drum)
Sittanavasal – Jain, now dated Pandya (9th c.)

traps: Sittanavasal paintings: notes say Pallava; standard books say Pandya

rows.v: Mahendravarman I – rock-cut halls (Mamandur, Trimurti Mandapa)
Narasimhavarman I – monolithic rathas, mandapas
Narasimhavarman II – structural (Shore, Kailasanatha)
Nandivarman II – small temples, decline
Fortified Vatapi (Badami) 543 CE; Ashvamedha
Extended the kingdom
Badami cave 3 (Vaishnava); lost civil war to nephew Pulakeshin II

keys.name: Pulakeshin II

rows.v: Beat him on the Narmada, 618 – 619
Dakshinapatheshvara (lord of the south)
Gave it to brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana – Eastern Chalukyas (c. 624)
Pullalur vs Mahendravarman I; killed when Narasimhavarman I took Vatapi (642)
Envoys with Khusrau II (c. 625) – Ajanta cave 1 mural
About 100 ships on the west coast
634 CE by Ravikirti (Jain) on the Meguti temple; Sanskrit; Ravikirti claims fame equal to Kalidasa and Bharavi
Hiuen Tsang praised him

traps: Ravikirti wrote; Pulakeshin II is praised
Chalukya rule was more central than Pallava village rule

rows.v: Won back Vatapi
Took Kanchi; queen Lokamahadevi built Virupaksha, Pattadakal
Last; overthrown by Dantidurga (Rashtrakuta) c. 753

keys.name: Chalukya art

rows.v: 4 rock-cut caves – 3 Hindu, 1 Jain
"Cradle of Indian temple architecture" – Lad Khan, apsidal Durga temple, Meguti
Both styles side by side – Papanatha (Nagara), Virupaksha (Dravida); UNESCO 1987
Vesara (mix) grows here

traps: Aihole = cradle, early; Pattadakal = mature, UNESCO
